jobs.title: Technical Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:

This person works with IT team members, business groups, and vendors to help translate business needs into practical, secure, and maintainable technical solutions. This role contributes to application development, system integrations, reporting, data management, automation, and emerging AI-enabled solutions under the guidance of senior technical resources and IT leadership.
Competitive Compensation Range:
$ 47.16/hr. to $53.85/hr. depending on experience
Essential Duties and Responsibilities

*Reasonable accommodation may be provided to enable qualified individuals to perform the essential functions.
Exercise a high level of professionalism and confidentiality when working with staff, projects, and proprietary information.
Develop, test, maintain, and support business applications and technical solutions.
Understand and extrapolate business needs and workflows and identify and recommend improved business processes and tools.
Build and maintain reusable services, APIs, scripts, and libraries that support business systems and integrations.
Build AI agents and/or other tools under the direction of the Senior Technical Solutions Engineer
Assist with the development and maintenance of data pipelines used to collect, transform, and store business data.
Support data models, reports, dashboards, and analytics solutions used by business teams.
Collaborate with IT and business stakeholders to support automation, AI-enabled tools, and workflow improvements.
Troubleshoot and resolve application and performance issues.
Administer relational and non-relational databases
Provide input on effort, technical complexity, and risks for assigned work and project planning.
Other duties as assigned.

Experience and Education

Bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent required.
4+ years’ experience in application development, database administration, data integrations, or related technical work in business environments.
Hands-on experience with one or more common programming languages, such as Python, JavaScript, .NET, C#, or VB.NET, is required.
Experience working with relational databases, including Microsoft SQL Server or MySQL, is required.
Experience supporting or maintaining system integrations using APIs, file transfers, or event-based processes.
Experience using, extending, and configuring the Microsoft Productivity Stack (Teams, SharePoint, Office 365, Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI, Copilot) is required.
Practical experience with data pipelines, analytics tools, AI-enabled tools, or automation solutions is preferred.
Working understanding of cloud platforms, Azure preferred, including compute, storage, and security concepts.
Experience with construction tools including Autodesk Construction Cloud,
Tekla, Viewpoint, Bluebeam and other applications used in manufacturing and construction are strongly preferred.

Core Values:

Determination:
Meet challenges head on!
Innovation:
Always look for better!
Well-Being:
Seek the success, health and happiness of all!
Benefits:

Competitive compensation, paid on a weekly basis.
Health, Dental and Vision Insurance with the options of using Kaiser and VSP for vision!
Medical FSA
Dependent Care FSA
Employer paid life insurance provided by Clark Pacific
Voluntary ancillary benefits such as Critical Illness, Accident Insurance, and Whole Life Insurance.

jobs.title: Environmental Data Specialist
jobs.description:
Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We're looking for an Environmental Data Specialist.
You will perform data entry and data management following established business processes to retrieve, verify, and maintain data generated during environmental site characterization, remediation, and monitoring activities. Work with database users, technical field teams, and contract laboratories to receive, assess, and process data; enhance data integrity, accessibility, and usability across one or more functional areas. The position is in the Program Services & Operations Division of the Environmental Restoration Department (ERD).

This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization.

You will

Perform data entry and data management following established business processes to retrieve, verify and maintain data generated during environmental site characterization, remediation, and monitoring activities.
Collaborate with stakeholders to define data requirements, reporting needs, and document them in clear specifications.
Work with technical staff to troubleshoot data issues, coordinate testing, and validate changes or enhancements to data systems and interfaces.
Develop and produce standard, recurring, and ad hoc reports, including data validation and explanation of trends or anomalies.
Assist in designing and implementing improvements to data collection, storage, and retrieval processes, including configuration of data management tools or applications.
Contribute to data-management documentation, including data dictionaries, standard operating procedures, records archives, and data-repositories, and support user training on data-entry standards, reporting tools, and data-management best practices.
Ensure chain-of-custody (COC) forms are complete, accurate, and timely and that the data from the analytical laboratories adhere to the contract.
Monitor data quality metrics and assist in developing controls, checks, and procedures to ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness of data.
Assist in developing environmental sampling plans and contributing to environmental regulatory reports.
Perform Technical Release Representative (TRR) duties to release work to outside vendors, commit substantial financial resources, and process and pay subcontract analytical laboratory invoices.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship.
Bachelor’s degree in business, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience.
Extensive knowledge of and experience with data management systems related to data entry and verification.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, accuracy, and follow through; experience with techniques for maintaining data integrity, error cause and effect analysis, and error prevention.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience to anticipate, identify, and resolve complex problems effectively.
Experience analyzing electronic data deliverables and creating standard and ad hoc reports.
Proven written and verbal communication skills necessary for effective interactions with all levels of personnel internal and external, regulatory agencies, and vendors, and experience working effectively independently and as a member of a team.
Knowledge of and experience using computer programs, system software and computer equipment, such as Microsoft Excel, Oracle based applications, SQL, Apple/Mac, and Linux operating systems.

Qualifications We Desire

Knowledge of LLNL procurement policies and procedures and best business practices.
Experience working with TEIMS, knowledge of SPACT, and ERD’s data repositories (i.e. Data Cave and Data Alley) and LLNL Records Management.
Familiarity with chemistry nomenclature to understand analytical laboratory test results.

Pay Range

$95,820 - $117,312 Annually

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Additional Information

Position Information

This is a Career Indefinite position, open to Lab employees and external candidates.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
Flexible Benefits Package
401(k)
Relocation Assistance
Education Reimbursement Program
Flexible schedules (*depending on project needs)
Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

Security Clearance

This position requires a Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance. If you are selected, we will initiate a Federal background investigation to determine if you meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information or matter. Also, all L or Q cleared employees are subject to random drug testing. Q-level clearance requires U.S. citizenship.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How To Identify Fake Job Advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

To learn more about recruitment scams: https://www.llnl.gov/sites/www/files/2023-05/LLNL-Job-Fraud-Statement-Updated-4.26.23.pdf

Equal Employment Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer that is committed to providing all with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, protected veteran status, age, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Reasonable Accommodation

Our goal is to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates applying and interviewing at the Laboratory. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please use our online form to submit a request.

California Privacy Notice

The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) grants privacy rights to all California residents. The law also entitles job applicants, employees, and non-employee workers to be notified of what personal information LLNL collects and for what purpose. The Employee Privacy Notice can be accessed here.

jobs.title: Research Data Analyst (School of Medicine Pediatric Infectious Diseases)
jobs.description:
About Our Client
The organization operates in the field of pediatric infectious disease research, focusing on improving treatment outcomes for children with tuberculosis (TB). It addresses challenges in pediatric TB care by conducting clinical trials and research studies designed to identify shorter, safer, and more effective treatment regimens. Its research programs involve collaboration across international clinical sites, expanding the reach and impact of its work.
About the Opportunity
The Research Data Analyst
supports data analysis and clinical research activities for studies including the SMART4TB TA2 Therapeutics study and the SMILE-TB trial. This role contributes to data collection, statistical analysis, reporting, and database management while applying clinical expertise to interpret pediatric TB research findings. The position also supports data quality, participant safety, and collaboration across multidisciplinary research teams.
Responsibilities
• Collect research data and generate reports, analytical models, and study findings.
• Run statistical models and prepare analytical reports for assigned research studies.
• Conduct data analyses supporting clinical research objectives and study outcomes.
• Use statistical software packages to analyze and interpret research data.
• Design tables and other formats to clearly present analytical results.
• Manage or assist with data entry and maintenance of research databases.
• Review, edit, and finalize study-related documents in collaboration with research teams.
• Review and summarize safety data, including adverse event reports.
• Provide clinical guidance regarding the management and interpretation of pediatric TB adverse events.
• Participate as a clinical expert in the Clinical Management Committee.
• Support data analysis teams by providing clinical interpretation of research findings.
• Generate, review, and resolve data queries within REDCap.
• Perform quality assurance activities to protect research participant rights, safety, and data integrity.
• Collaborate with investigators, data management teams, and clinical research personnel as needed.
• Perform additional research and analytical duties as assigned.
Requirements
• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline.
• Minimum of three years of related professional experience; additional education may substitute in accordance with applicable equivalency guidelines.
• Three years of direct patient care experience in resource-limited hospital settings.
• Proficiency with STATA and/or R, REDCap, EndNote, Microsoft Word, and Microsoft Excel.
• Strong analytical and data interpretation skills.
• Ability to apply clinical knowledge to research data analysis and safety assessments.
• Preferred experience diagnosing and treating pediatric TB in low-resource settings.
• Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.
Pay Range and Compensation Package
• Starting hourly salary range of $25.23–$44.20
, with a targeted rate of $43.00 per hour
, commensurate with experience.

The Lead Project Coordinator supports new store opening initiatives for a multi-banner retail organization. This role coordinates multiple fixture, equipment, and signage installations each quarter, partnering with store and field leadership, Construction, IT, Finance, Fixture Purchasing, Store Planning, and other cross-functional teams to deliver operational support, execute business processes, and maintain up-to-date documentation including timelines, procedures, manuals, and training materials. The Lead Coordinator drives projects against approved plans, proactively identifies and resolves issues, and applies best practices to minimize shortages, go-backs, and rework while delivering a high level of service to stores.

Project Planning & Coordination
Develop and maintain project timelines and budgets, including project plans, stakeholder communications, and supporting documentation for operational procedures.
Manage schedules and track project milestones to ensure on-time completion across multiple concurrent store openings.
Support pre-opening preparations, including reviewing fixture plans, confirming fixture orders, and issuing plans to installers for scheduled installations.

Vendor & Installer Management
Coordinate requests for installer bids and analyze submittals for leadership review.
Review site conditions and municipal delivery constraints, partnering with logistics vendors to ensure on-time delivery of fixtures, equipment, and signage.
Manage vendor follow-up, oversee new store kit assembly (including print/copy center requests and packing), and code financial invoices.

Communication & Process Improvement
Support and contribute to field-facing conference calls and update related materials.
Create new store survey questions for touch-base calls with field teams.
Support process improvement initiatives across the new store opening workflow.

Qualifications

Retail store operations experience.
Extensive coordination and project management experience, preferably in retail.
Strong cross-functional collaboration and vendor management background.
Demonstrated experience managing schedules and tracking project timelines to on-time completion.
Strong analytical skills with advanced Microsoft Excel proficiency required (formulas, pivot tables, data analysis).
Proficiency in the broader Microsoft Office Suite (especially Word) and Smartsheet.
Highly detail-oriented with the ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

As a Tagging and Inventory Technician, you’ll be responsible for performing inspections on various types of facilities in the Oil and Gas Industry to identify and quantify hydrocarbon gas leaks and vents at offshore facilities.

The compensation range for this role is $21 - $23/hr. commensurate with experience, skills, and geographic location.

To thrive in this role, you’ll be comfortable taking ownership of the following responsibilities:

Assisting in coordinating and navigating to various facilities with maps and GPS
Helping to calibrate and maintain equipment
Using various detection and measurement technologies under the supervision of the Team Lead
Collecting and recording emission data
Preparing field reports as required

Your Expertise And Skills

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

Experience in Oil and Gas industry (preference given to candidates with natural gas processing/transmission facility experience)
Effective computer skills (Excel and Microsoft Office are essential) and proficiency with Android OS
Experience leading a team preferred/required, depending on the position
Must be able to communicate clearly and precisely
Offshore and/or military experience is a plus.
Valid driver's license
Preference will be given to candidates with an associate or bachelor's degree in engineering technology or applicable technical degree/diploma; related work experience in hydrocarbon detection and measurement, LDAR, Offshore, instrumentation or stack emission testing or a mechanical background are also preferred, but not required

Must be able to safely ascend and descend structures up to approximately 200 feet in height and remain physically capable of performing required job duties after climbing
Position requires significant physical exertion, including climbing stairs and ladders, carrying heavy equipment, working at heights, and potentially working in confined spaces
Ability to pass pre-employment drug screen and background check

The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding a GIS Analyst to our GIS team based in Buffalo, NY.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

Tetra Tech is currently seeking a motivated, articulate and dynamic, middle to senior level GIS Analyst to support our natural resources projects and programs. The successful candidate will have experience with GIS, cloud infrastructure, and computer science experience. They should be comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, supporting multiple projects in a team setting. A willingness to learn existing systems, templates, and workflows as well as improve these processes. This individual will be detail oriented and will be asked to manage extremely large datasets within the confines of stringent agreements with clients.

The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting a variety of natural resources projects, with a primary focus on GIS analysis/mapping, GIS data management in a cloud system, and produce technical reports. The candidate will generally support senior-level staff with GIS analysis/mapping, report writing, and technical support.

Essential Job Functions

Candidate will be required to act as a GIS analyst for projects with an ecological services component and other duties as assigned. The successful candidate with appropriate work ethic for the industry and position will assist with environmental surveys, reporting, and permitting processes. Additionally, as required by the supervisor, the successful candidate will work overtime and/or weekends. Essential duties include the following:

Take complex ideas, convert them to User Experiences and visualize them in User Interfaces and workflow diagrams. Translate those ideas into actionable steps in an Agile Scrum technology focused work environment.
Support Microsoft cloud infrastructure support like Virtual Machines, Azure SQL, Azure SQL with SDE, Azure Blob Storage, Azure Apps and Functions.
Support the development of SharePoint Sites with custom JavaScript Code inside iFrames and PowerApps.
Write Python and JavaScript code for data management, QA/QC, and automation opportunities between GIS and Non-GIS applications as well as field mobile data collection apps.
Identify and implement permission management in Azure, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
Maintain and catalog field GPS and Mobile Data Collection equipment and protocol with a virtual Mobile Device Management system.
Work directly with the Technical Services Manager, and with other project managers and personnel to support business tasks like:
Assist in supporting the permitting of large-scale energy generation projects.
Preparation of figures for permits.
GIS analysis for above ground risk mitigation.
Technical report writing.
Data compilation and analysis for report writing, permit application preparation, and plant community mapping.
Identify published sources and downloading of spatial data in support of natural resources projects.
Set up, collect, download, and post-process GPS data from a wide range of sources.

Required Qualifications

B.A. or B.S in Geosciences, Geography, GIS, or similar field.
5+ years of experience in GIS applicable role that required GIS to be used more than 50% of the work week.
1+ year Azure Cloud experience.
Basic working knowledge of computer science and its application to Python, JavaScript, and git repo management.
A pre-employment drug screen in compliance with state regulations is required.
Must possess a valid Driver's License with a clean driving record without restrictions.

Preferred Qualifications

Masters Degree in GIS.
Geographer or Equivalent.
10+ years experience.
Proposal Support.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Fully Remote – Visits required to Tetra Tech offices in Buffalo, Pittsburgh, Houston, etc.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Strong knowledge of the ArcGIS platform and other relevant GIS software.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain GIS applications.
Experience in scripting and automation of GIS tasks.
Familiarity with current GIS technology trends and the ability to integrate innovative solutions into workflows.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
Proven experience working with clients, addressing their GIS needs and troubleshooting issues.
Capability to mentor and guide junior team members.

Advanced expertise in the ArcGIS suite, including ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, and ArcGIS Enterprise.
Familiarity with field data collection and management techniques.
Experience with scripting languages such as Python for GIS automation.
Experience consulting within the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction industry.
Experience working on renewables, transmission, land development, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience using AutoCAD and DWG files.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding experienced Cost Estimators to our Disaster Recovery team to support current and future disaster recovery operations across the United States.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world's most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential - join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

This is an on-call, as-needed cadre position. Work assignments are not guaranteed and depend on disaster declarations, contract awards, client needs, project requirements, qualifications, availability, and recovery program activations.
Acceptance of assignments is voluntary, and periods of inactivity between deployments may occur.
Assignment schedules may be flexible and may include periods of high-intensity workload during active recovery operations.
Some deployments may require extended travel or mobilization on short notice; other assignments may be fully remote.
Evening and weekend work may be required during surge events or active disaster recovery operations.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Explore our open positions at https://www.tetratech.com/careers. Follow us on social media to learn more about our people, culture, and opportunities:

LinkedIn: @TetraTechCareers

X (Twitter): @TetraTechJobs

jobs.description:
Responsibilities

This is for an upcoming future opportunity. This position is part of a proposal effort and is contingent upon contract award. This will be based out of Bethesda, MD.

The Scientist (UNDS) provides scientific research, biological analysis, and technical support to the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCDD) in the area of Uniform National Discharge Standards (UNDS) program execution. This role applies biological science expertise to support the Navy's compliance with 40 CFR 1700 and related state, federal, and international wastewater management policies affecting Navy vessels and operations.

This position applies scientific methodology, including biological sampling, toxicity testing, bioassay methods, and EPA-approved test methods (40 CFR 136), to discharge characterization, water quality analysis, and regulatory impact assessment. The Scientist coordinates with EPA, state regulatory agencies, Navy program offices, and Fleet units to support requirements development, discharge characterization, and policy compliance for the Navy's UNDS program. The candidate is responsible for UNDS task areas and must apply rigorous QA/QC protocols, laboratory information management systems (LIMS), and Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater to ensure scientifically defensible results.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities (UNDS Support) Include

Review state, federal, and international policies and regulations affecting shipboard wastewater discharge management
Summarize regulatory findings in clear, actionable scientific reports for program leadership and stakeholders
Identify and assess the impacts of proposed or enacted regulatory changes on Navy UNDS program compliance obligations
Monitor EPA rulemaking, Congressional legislation, and international conventions (e.g., MARPOL Annex IV) for UNDS relevance
Characterize discharges from Navy vessels using biological sampling, chemical analysis, and physical measurements per 40 CFR Part 1700
Conduct biological sampling, toxicity testing, and bioassay methods to assess discharge characteristics and environmental impacts
Apply EPA-approved test methods (40 CFR 136) and Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater for all analytical work
Collect and analyze water quality data from discharge streams aboard Navy vessels; maintain chain of custody and QA/QC protocols
Support preparation of discharge characterization reports and data summaries (CDRL A002)
Coordinate with laboratories and field teams for sampling and analytical services as required; utilize LIMS for data management
Support the development of Navy regulations, policies, and guidelines in response to UNDS requirements
Draft and review UNDS-related policy documents, standards, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) drawing on biological science expertise
Coordinate with NAVSEA, EPA, and Navy program offices to develop scientifically sound regulatory responses
Assist in the preparation of Navy comments on proposed federal and state environmental rulemakings affecting biological and water quality standards
Conduct outreach and awareness training for Navy personnel on UNDS requirements, discharge standards, and compliance procedures
Develop training materials, presentations, and informational resources on biological sampling and water quality for Fleet and program office audiences
Support creation of awareness campaigns and educational content related to shipboard environmental stewardship and discharge management
Deliver training in multiple formats including classroom, aboard ship, and through informational products
Manage supporting documentation arising from UNDS regulatory, policy, sampling, and outreach activities
Track actions and decisions resulting from regulatory reviews, policy development, laboratory analyses, and program meetings
Maintain program records, laboratory data files, and correspondence related to UNDS compliance activities
Prepare status reports and action item logs for program leadership review; ensure QA/QC documentation is current and complete
Plan, coordinate, and attend program reviews, conferences, symposia, and other programmatic and technical meetings related to UNDS work
Prepare agendas, scientific presentation materials, and meeting minutes for UNDS-related events
Represent NSWCDD UNDS program at interagency, Fleet, and external stakeholder forums as appropriate
Track and follow up on action items arising from meetings and technical exchanges
Provide analytical services for laboratory and shipboard/pier-side testing of water and wastewater quality and characterization
Conduct water and wastewater sampling in accordance with EPA-approved test methods (40 CFR 136) and Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater
Perform biological, chemical, and physical analytical testing and analyses using calibrated laboratory equipment and instrumentation
Apply statistical validation and QA/QC protocols to all analytical data; document results in LIMS and prepare analytical reports
Support whole effluent toxicity (WET) testing and bioassay studies for discharge characterization
Conduct studies on shipboard environmental systems and shore-side discharge operations
Perform legislative reviews, rulemaking analyses, and international treaty reviews relevant to biological water quality standards
Analyze regulatory documents for their impact and relevance to Navy programs and UNDS compliance
Draft standards and regulations; prepare supporting scientific presentations and briefing materials
Provide scientific data analysis, interpretation of laboratory results, and statistical projections related to discharge characterization and biological sampling
Support UNDS compliance data reporting, trend analysis, and QA/QC reviews of analytical data
Prepare data summaries, charts, and visualizations for program reports and briefings
Write, review, edit, provide comments on, and revise scientific and technical documents including laboratory reports, sampling plans, and SOPs
Develop technical assessments and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for biological sampling and analytical procedures
Review and develop drawings; rewrite/incorporate revisions into existing documents
Attend technical and programmatic meetings; provide minutes and track action items to completion
Arrange, organize, coordinate, schedule, and facilitate events including meetings, program reviews, and symposia
Design and develop informational posters, brochures, specification sheets, and scientific outreach materials

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Biology from an accredited College or University

Shall possess at least approximately five (5) years of experience in work related to Uniform National Discharge Standards (UNDS) and its impact on Navy operations and vessels
Expert knowledge of the Uniform National Discharge Standards (UNDS) regulatory framework under 40 CFR Part 1700, and the underlying Clean Water Act (33 U.S.C.
1322) authorities governing vessel discharges of the Armed Forces
Strong foundation in biology, including microbiology, aquatic biology, or marine biology, as applied to water quality analysis, discharge characterization, biological sampling, and assessment of environmental impacts from shipboard discharges
Proficiency in water and wastewater sampling techniques; skilled in applying EPA-approved test methods (40 CFR 136) and Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater for all laboratory and field analyses
Experience with biological sampling, toxicity testing, and bioassay methods (including whole effluent toxicity testing) to characterize vessel discharge streams and assess biological impacts on receiving water bodies
Demonstrated experience implementing QA/QC protocols in laboratory and field settings; proficiency with Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), chain of custody documentation, and laboratory equipment calibration and maintenance
Proficiency in scientific data analysis, statistical validation, and interpretation of laboratory results; ability to apply quantitative methods to support UNDS compliance reporting and discharge characterization studies
Familiarity with federal environmental statutes (Clean Water Act, NEPA) and international treaties (MARPOL 73/78 Annex IV) applicable to ship waste management and discharge regulation; ability to assess regulatory impacts on Navy biological testing programs
Knowledge of OPNAV-M 5090.1 (Environmental Readiness Program Manual) and relevant Navy environmental policy documents governing shipboard environmental compliance and biological monitoring requirements
Strong scientific writing skills fProficiency with MS Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), LIMS, scientific databases, and data analysis tools
preparation of sampling plans, laboratory reports, technical assessments, and regulatory analyses
ability to communicate complex biological and technical findings to diverse stakeholders
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance

Job Description

This Opportunity

At WSP, you can access our global scale while contributing to meaningful projects that help shape the future of communities and the environment. We are currently initiating a search for a Wetland Delineator/Environmental Scientist for our Cincinnati, Columbus, Cleveland, Dayton, Akron, Toledo, Indianapolis, or other regional offices.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a collaborative team of environmental professionals supporting infrastructure, utility, and renewable energy projects throughout the Midwest. At WSP, we are driven by a shared purpose to create positive, lasting impacts through innovative environmental solutions and sustainable project delivery.

As part of our Environmental Science team, you'll work alongside industry-leading experts who are passionate about protecting natural resources while helping clients navigate complex environmental challenges. We foster a culture that values technical excellence, collaboration, continuous learning, and professional growth, empowering our people to build rewarding and impactful careers.

Your Impact

Assist with planning and execution of wetland delineations and stream assessments.
Perform duties as a wetland field team lead in accordance with current USACE 1987 Manual and Regional Supplements. Potential to support other natural resource surveys as needed.
Understand how to operate a GPS unit to collect field data, map habitat types and sensitive resources.
Support preparation of field equipment, mapping, Safe Work Plans, and logistics for field work.
Perform data entry, data analysis and report compilation.
Assist with various governmental agency coordination (USFWS, USACE, OEPA, ODNR, etc.).
Assist and lead preparation of wetland delineation reports and permit applications for federal and/or state environmental permits, including USACE Section 404 and Section 10, state wetland and stream permits, and NPDES compliance.
Field projects may require long hours and/or be physically demanding, and may require being on foot 10-12 hours per day traversing various topography while carrying equipment in varying weather conditions.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

3+ years of experience conducting wetland delineations and stream assessments, preferably in Ohio and surrounding states.
Bachelors of Arts or Bachelors of Science degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Environmental Studies, Biology or related field.
Familiarity with USACE wetland data forms, ORAM wetland data forms, and QHEI and HHEI stream data forms.
Experience with GPS field data collection.
Plant identification of Midwest vegetation.
Willingness to learn and implement various field methods for collection of data.
Proficient with data management, organization and MS Office Suite.
Attention and commitment to timely completion of high-quality work, often independently motivated.
Flexibility and adaptability to meet fast-paced demands.
Willing to work long hours in the field for two weeks a month or more during peak periods of fieldwork.
High level of motivation and an ability to work as a team lead or independently as part of various teams.
Positive attitude and willingness to learn.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s and client-specific health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience as a team lead for a wetland delineation crew.
Experience with use of ArcOnline, and ArcCollector or other field data collection applications.
Strong technical writing skills, clear communicator, ability to work as part of multidisciplinary teams, and attention to detail.
Knowledge of USACE Section 401/404 permitting, Section 10 permitting and mitigation requirements.

jobs.description:
Required Skills:

Strong SQL, Databricks ( or Snowflake) , Python and PowerBI (reports and dashboard development)

Snowflake, Python

Description:

We are seeking a highly analytical, technically strong, and relentlessly curious Data Analyst / Analytics Engineer to help transform complex, disconnected data into trusted business insights and scalable data solutions.
While strong SQL skills remain essential, success in this role requires a broader capability across Databricks, data engineering, end-to-end analytics, and Power BI development. This role is not limited to querying data—it requires building and optimizing the data foundation, shaping business-ready datasets, and delivering clear, executive-ready reporting and visualization solutions.
The ideal candidate is equally comfortable working across raw data, transformation logic, analytical modeling, and front-end reporting. They enjoy solving difficult problems, thrive in ambiguity, and continuously ask questions to understand not only what happened, but also why it happened, where the data came from, how it should be modeled, and how insights should be delivered to the business in a trusted and scalable way.
This individual should be able to work across the full analytics lifecycle: sourcing and engineering data, understanding lineage and dependencies, designing curated datasets, applying business logic, validating outputs, and delivering insights through dashboards, reports, and executive readouts. They are naturally driven to investigate, learn the business, understand source systems, and uncover relationships across domains that others may overlook.
This role supports strategic business initiatives across Fiber, Connected Communities, Mobility, customer, revenue, operational, and financial domains. The individual is expected to partner closely with business stakeholders, develop a deep understanding of the business, and create scalable, trusted, and well-engineered data and reporting solutions that support executive decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:

Analyze and integrate data across multiple applications, source systems, and business domains.
Design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines and transformation logic to support analytics and reporting needs.
Develop advanced SQL queries, analytical models, and reconciliation logic to investigate, validate, and unify complex datasets.
Use Databricks to engineer, transform, optimize, and operationalize large-scale datasets for analytical consumption.
Build curated, business-ready datasets that serve as trusted sources for analysis, executive reporting, and self-service consumption.
Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and reports that translate complex data into clear, actionable insights for business and executive stakeholders.
Own analytics solutions end to end, from raw data ingestion and transformation through semantic logic, reporting, visualization, and insight generation.
Transform fragmented and complex data into clear, business-relevant stories and recommendations.
Identify relationships between customers, products, locations, revenue, operational activity, and business performance.
Partner with business stakeholders to understand objectives, define KPIs and metrics, and solve challenging business problems.
Investigate data quality issues, perform root-cause analysis, and implement sustainable fixes in partnership with upstream and downstream teams.
Ensure data lineage, business logic, and transformation rules are documented, scalable, and maintainable.
Improve performance, reliability, and usability of analytical workflows using modern engineering and BI best practices.
Continuously expand business, source system, platform, and reporting knowledge to accelerate problem-solving and improve analytical effectiveness.

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role
The strongest individuals in this role are not simply SQL developers, report builders, or dashboard creators. They are end-to-end problem solvers who can connect business needs, data engineering, analytics, and reporting into scalable solutions.
They:
Possess strong analytical curiosity and a desire to deeply understand how the business works.
Have hands-on experience with Databricks, modern data transformation, and analytical data engineering.
Have strong Power BI skills and know how to turn complex analysis into intuitive, executive-friendly dashboards and reporting.
Can connect disparate pieces of information into a complete, accurate, and actionable story.
Are comfortable working through ambiguity and incomplete requirements.
Ask thoughtful questions and challenge assumptions.
Take ownership of finding the right answer, not just the quickest answer.
Understand that trusted analytics begin with well-engineered, validated, and well-modeled data.
Can move seamlessly from raw data to business-ready insight and visualization.
Continuously build expertise in business processes, data lineage, system dependencies, and analytical modeling.
Translate complex technical findings into clear business recommendations and executive-ready outputs.
Demonstrate persistence, intellectual curiosity, and a passion for learning.
Balance speed with rigor, ensuring that solutions are both actionable and sustainable.

Qualifications
Strong SQL development and data analysis experience.
Strong hands-on experience with Databricks for large-scale data processing, transformation, and analytics.
Experience designing and maintaining data pipelines, transformation workflows, and curated analytical datasets.
Strong experience with Power BI (PBI) for dashboard development, data modeling, visualization, and business reporting.
Strong understanding of data engineering concepts, including data lineage, data quality, transformation logic, and scalable data modeling.
Experience working with large and complex datasets across multiple systems.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Ability to investigate and reconcile data across multiple platforms and source systems.
Experience supporting end-to-end analytics, from raw data ingestion to reporting, dashboarding, and insight generation.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to translate business questions into technical, analytical, and reporting solutions.
Preferred
Experience with Snowflake, Python, Spark, Terraform, or enterprise data warehouse environments.
Experience with modern cloud-based analytics platforms and data engineering frameworks.
Knowledge of telecommunications, customer, revenue, operational, or financial data domains.
Experience working with cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment.
Familiarity with KPI governance, executive reporting, and semantic layer design.

Databricks, data engineering capability, Power BI expertise, analytical curiosity, and business understanding determine your success.
The best people in this role become trusted advisors because they understand the business, understand the data, and know how to engineer scalable solutions and deliver trusted insights through effective reporting. They do not simply build reports—they build reliable data foundations, create meaningful visualizations, uncover insights, solve complex problems, and help the organization make better decisions through end-to-end analytics

to join our Growth team and support MobilityWare’
s portfolio of mobile games. In this role, your primary focus will be partnering closely with teams across User Acquisition (UA)
, Creative, Product, and Finance to help drive smart, data-informed growth decisions.

This role is specifically focused on User Acquisition and Growth Analytics within mobile gaming
. We’re primarily seeking candidates with mobile gaming experience and a strong interest in UA and growth marketing.

This is much more than a reporting role. We’re looking for someone who enjoys digging into complex data, identifying meaningful trends and opportunities, and translating insights into clear recommendations that influence strategy. The ideal candidate is both analytical and collaborative, someone who can think critically about performance, communicate insights clearly, and build strong partnerships across teams.

You’ll play an important role in shaping acquisition strategy across channels such as Google Ads, Apple Search Ads, Meta, and other ad networks. From campaign performance and creative testing to monetization trends and growth forecasting, your insights will help guide decisions across multiple game titles.

Responsibilities:

Partner closely with the User Acquisition team across 2–4 mobile game titles to drive growth through thoughtful, data-informed decision-making
Analyze UA performance data to identify trends, opportunities, risks, and key drivers impacting growth and efficiency
Deliver clear, actionable insights and recommendations around campaign optimization, audience targeting, bidding strategies, creative performance, and budget allocation
Evaluate key performance metrics including ROAS, CPI, retention, LTV, payback periods, and install growth
Design and analyze A/B tests across creative concepts, acquisition channels, targeting strategies, and app store optimization efforts

Work cross-functionally with Product, Finance, and Data teams to connect acquisition performance with broader business goals
Build and improve dashboards, reporting frameworks, and analytical tools that help teams make faster, more informed decisions
Conduct competitive and market analysis to identify emerging trends and growth opportunities
Present findings and recommendations clearly and effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Bring structure, curiosity, and strong analytical thinking to open-ended and ambiguous business questions

ABOUT BEACON DATA
As a full-stack data and growth consulting firm, Beacon leverages machine and human intelligence to help clients achieve breakthrough performance. Organizations don’t just call us to architect smart data strategy – they call us to implement it. As their expert data partner, our cross-functional team parachutes in to optimize data environments, unify fragmented data, and operationalize AI/ML use cases that accelerate growth. At Beacon, impact goes beyond improving the bottom line: one in four of our clients are mission-based organizations.

Stitching together tens of millions of airline customer records to increase loyalty program enrollment
Predicting optimal inventory levels for a supply chain firm to reduce idle time
Optimizing donor targeting for a leading children’s hospital using advanced segmentation
Designing and implementing a modern analytics platform for the largest online theater ticketing company
Applying ML/AI to optimize contact strategies and improve credit card debt recovery outcomes

THE ROLE

Beacon Data is seeking a Senior Data Analyst
to join our data team and support high-impact analytics and business intelligence work for our clients. This is a senior, hands-on analytics role focused on transforming complex data into trusted insights, scalable reporting, and clear recommendations for decision-makers.

You will work closely with Beacon project leads, data architects, and client stakeholders to shape analytics requirements, build robust data models, and deliver insights that directly inform strategy and operations.

Qualifications

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS (MUST HAVES)

3+ years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, or related roles
Advanced proficiency in SQL for analysis and analytics data modeling
Experience building dashboards and reports in BI tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar
Experience working with modern data transformation or orchestration tools (e.g., dbt, ADF, SSIS, Airflow)
Working knowledge of Python for data analysis, automation, or advanced analytics tasks
Experience operating within cloud data environments (AWS or Azure; Snowflake preferred)
Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills
Eligibility to work in the United States

Preferred Qualifications (nice To Haves)

Experience mentoring or guiding junior analysts
Strong understanding of relational database principles and data modeling
Experience working with CRM, ERP, marketing, or operational systems
Comfort working with structured and semi-structured data sources
Client-facing experience, including presenting insights to non-technical audiences
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
High attention to detail and commitment to high-quality analytics outputs

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Beacon Data is seeking a talented, Business Intelligence Analyst/ Engineer to join our data team and help us solve complex and interesting problems for our diverse clients. During your initial project, you and your engagement team will assist with building a new data reporting and data orchestration system for several clients.

Your Team Will

Lead the development of analytics-ready datasets and metrics that serve as a single source of truth
Analyze data from ERP, CRM, and other operational systems to answer complex business questions
Write and maintain production-quality SQL to transform, validate, and analyze data
Build and maintain dashboards and reports in BI tools that support executive and operational decision-making
Partner with business stakeholders to translate questions and hypotheses into structured analyses
Identify trends, patterns, and anomalies in data and communicate insights clearly
Support and collaborate on data pipeline and transformation work alongside data engineers and analytics engineers
Ensure data accuracy, consistency, documentation, and adherence to security best practices

You will work under the strategic guidance of Beacon’s Senior Data Architect and receive day-to-day support from an experienced Senior Project Lead. You will collaborate closely with Beacon teammates and client-side analysts, engineers, and IT partners in an agile, team-based environment.

This is a highly collaborative role focused on building analytics solutions that enable better decision-making across organizations.

WHO YOU ARE
You are a curious, collaborative, and impact-driven analyst who enjoys turning complex data into clear insights. You value thoughtful problem-solving, continuous improvement, and working closely with others to deliver meaningful results. You thrive in dynamic environments and enjoy balancing technical rigor with business context.

jobs.description:
Merge is the leading provider of agentic tools and customer-facing integrations for frontier LLMs, Fortune 500 organizations, and B2B SaaS companies. Our platform offers three core products: Merge Unified, which enables businesses to add hundreds of integrations to their products with a single API, Merge Agent Handler, which empowers AI agents with secure access to thousands of third-party tools, and Merge Gateway, the control plane for running AI in production. Merge's enterprise-grade platform handles the entire integration lifecycle, from authentication and security to monitoring and maintenance. Thousands of companies trust Merge to accelerate product development, unblock sales, reduce customer churn, and save engineering resources—allowing them to focus on their core product.

Who are we looking for?

We're a high-growth Series B company selling into a fast-moving AI and developer ecosystem where the market changes weekly and a finding that's interesting today is table stakes in a month. We move quickly, we work hard, and we care a great deal about being right.

We're hiring a Data Analyst to find the insights that drive our growth. You'll work directly with leadership on product and market strategy, shape how we make decisions as an engineering team, and influence how Merge presents itself to the world. If you want to dig into data no one has looked at, find the thing worth saying, and have your analysis be the reason we went left instead of right, this is the role.

What will you be doing?

Dig into our product, customer, and market data to find patterns worth acting on and raise questions before anyone else discovers them.
Work with engineering and design to build dashboards and frontend analytics that give customers a reliable view of what's happening in the product.
Partner with product marketing and sales to turn findings into campaigns, launch assets, and the numbers behind the pitch + the methodology to back them up.
Field requests from across the business and decide what warrants a deep dive, a quick pass, or a later response.
Analyze product usage data (onboarding funnels, feature adoption, dashboard engagement) to identify opportunities to improve the customer journey.
Turn one-off analyses into repeatable internal tools and self-service resources so the next request is faster than the last.

What experience is required?

Degree in data science, computer science, statistics, or a similar quantitative field.
2+ years in analytics, data science, insights, or a technical GTM / BizOps role.
Strong SQL. You write clean, structured queries on large datasets, and whether you wrote them yourself or an AI assistant did, you own the correctness of every result before it reaches a stakeholder.
Working knowledge of dbt. You'll use and extend existing models without needing to own a full warehouse build.
Working Python for analysis and automation, including AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual reporting overhead.
Writing that carries a finding. You can take an analysis and produce something a marketer, a seller, or a customer reads once and understands.

Nice to have

Experience at a B2B SaaS or developer tools company, or anywhere with a real data asset
Background working closely with product, marketing, sales, and/or revenue operations
Hands-on experience with product analytics tools like PostHog, Mixpanel, or Amplitude.
Familiarity with LLM and AI infrastructure data, or a genuine interest in learning it fast

Compensation

The cash compensation range for this role is $150,000-170,000
Actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications. In addition to cash compensation, all employees receive an equity compensation package.

The Mechanical Project Coordinator is responsible for supporting the Mechanical Change Order Estimating team by coordinating project information, assisting with estimate preparation, and ensuring accurate and timely project deliverables. Position Responsibilities

Support the Mechanical Change Order Estimating team throughout the estimating process by coordinating project information and maintaining estimating timelines.

Review construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents to assist with quantity takeoffs and estimate preparation.

Communicate with customers and internal project teams to define project scope, resolve deficiencies, and support pricing efforts.
Maintain organized estimating files, track project milestones, and ensure deliverables are completed on schedule.

Continuously develop knowledge of mechanical systems, estimating processes, and Power Design's preconstruction operations.

Ability to multitask in a high-volume, fast-paced work environment while managing competing priorities.

The organization operates in the field of pediatric infectious disease research, focusing on improving treatment outcomes for children with tuberculosis (TB). The Research Data Analyst
supports data analysis and clinical research activities for studies including the SMART4TB TA2 Therapeutics study and the SMILE-TB trial. new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding experienced Cost Estimators to our Disaster Recovery team to support current and future disaster recovery operations across the United States.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world's most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential - join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
